objective: Test whether a Bishop-inspired per-96-bit-tile density router between a dense sequential bypass and the existing shared-state K8 sparse FC2 frontend has at least 1.10x ideal same-bandwidth opportunity on frozen Motion/H67 ep35 payloads before any RTL is authorized.

comparison.strong_baseline: sealed M216 full-vector K8 always-ready standalone sparse-FC2 frontend
comparison.candidate: per-96-bit density route to dense sequential bypass or K8 sparse compactor
comparison.same_resource: eight logical weight banks, at most one source per bank per cycle
comparison.sparse_tile_floor: maximum nonzero count among the eight modulo-8 banks

decision_gate.if_both_pass: authorize only a minimum route-bit plus dense-counter RTL proposal; VCS/DC remain separate gates

literature_mechanism_only.Bishop: ISCA 2025 dense/sparse TTB stratifier; published speedups are not transferred
literature_mechanism_only.FireFly_T: 2025 multi-lane nonzero decoder and bank-aware load balancing; published FPGA metrics are not transferred
